index fef54033db..d425730d41 100755
--- a/bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py
+++ b/bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py
@@ -294,6 +294,104 @@ class PresenceCompletenessTest(unittest.TestCase):
         self.assertIn("**Attempted: 2 trials produced a result.json", report)
 
 
+class ShardCompletenessGuardTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """gh-1658 C3 — the aggregate fails loudly on a zero-trial shard.
+
+    A shard that vanished from the merged artifacts (startup crash, lost
+    upload) must not silently shrink the resolution denominator: for every
+    expected shard (the workflow passes `--expected-shards N`, N = the
+    setup matrix length) the merged export must carry >= 1 readable
+    result.json keyed to that shard's index (the job-name suffix). The
+    guard is additive: without `--expected-shards` the legacy shape is
+    byte-identical.
+    """
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        self._summary_bak = os.environ.pop("GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY", None)
+        self._label_bak = os.environ.pop("BENCH_RUN_LABEL", None)
+        self.addCleanup(self._restore_env)
+        tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(tmp.cleanup)
+        self.jobs = Path(tmp.name)
+
+    def _restore_env(self):
+        if self._summary_bak is not None:
+            os.environ["GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"] = self._summary_bak
+        if self._label_bak is not None:
+            os.environ["BENCH_RUN_LABEL"] = self._label_bak
+
+    def _run(self, *argv) -> tuple[int, str]:
+        out = io.StringIO()
+        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out):
+            rc = main(list(argv))
+        return rc, out.getvalue()
+
+    def test_all_shards_contributing_passes(self):
+        make_jobs(self.jobs, "fa-2.1-docker-cpu-0", [{"resolved": True}, {"resolved": False}])
+        make_jobs(self.jobs, "fa-2.1-docker-cpu-1", [{"resolved": True}])
+        rc, out = self._run(str(self.jobs), "--family", "2.1", "--expected-shards", "2")
+        self.assertEqual(rc, 0)
+        self.assertNotIn("contributed 0 trials", out)
+
+    def test_vanished_shard_fails_named(self):
+        # Shard 1 uploaded nothing: no dir at all in the merged export.
+        make_jobs(self.jobs, "fa-2.1-docker-cpu-0", [{"resolved": True}])
+        rc, out = self._run(str(self.jobs), "--family", "2.1", "--expected-shards", "2")
+        self.assertEqual(rc, 1)
+        self.assertIn("- shard 1: 0 trials", out)
+        self.assertIn("contributed 0 trials to the merged export", out)
+
+    def test_present_but_empty_shard_fails_named(self):
+        # The dir survived the artifact merge but carries no readable
+        # result.json — it contributes 0 trials all the same.
+        make_jobs(self.jobs, "fa-2.1-docker-cpu-0", [{"resolved": True}])
+        (self.jobs / "fa-2.1-docker-cpu-1").mkdir()
+        (self.jobs / "fa-2.1-docker-cpu-1" / "trial-0").mkdir()
+        rc, out = self._run(str(self.jobs), "--family", "2.1", "--expected-shards", "2")
+        self.assertEqual(rc, 1)
+        self.assertIn("- shard 1: 0 trials", out)
+
+    def test_shard_index_parse_is_exact_not_a_suffix_match(self):
+        # `shard 11` must never satisfy `shard 1`: the index is the
+        # job-name's trailing dash-segment, not a string suffix.
+        make_jobs(self.jobs, "fa-2.1-docker-cpu-0", [{"resolved": True}])
+        make_jobs(self.jobs, "fa-2.1-docker-cpu-11", [{"resolved": True}])
+        rc, out = self._run(str(self.jobs), "--family", "2.1", "--expected-shards", "12")
+        self.assertEqual(rc, 1)
+        self.assertIn("- shard 1: 0 trials", out)
+        self.assertIn("- shard 10: 0 trials", out)
+        self.assertNotIn("- shard 11: 0 trials", out)
+
+    def test_guard_is_additive_without_the_flag(self):
+        # Legacy invocations (no --expected-shards) keep their verdict:
+        # a missing shard only shrinks the report, never fails it.
+        make_jobs(self.jobs, "fa-2.1-docker-cpu-0", [{"resolved": True}])
+        rc, out = self._run(str(self.jobs), "--family", "2.1")
+        self.assertEqual(rc, 0)
+        self.assertNotIn("0 trials", out)
+
+    def test_ledger_row_caveat_names_the_lost_denominator(self):
+        # The paste-ready docs/bench.md row must not ride a shrunken
+        # denominator silently — same discipline as the gh-1579 caveat.
+        make_jobs(self.jobs, "fa-2.1-docker-cpu-0", [{"resolved": True}])
+        rc, out = self._run(
+            str(self.jobs), "--family", "2.1", "--model", "glm-5.3-flash",
+            "--fa-ref", "abc1234", "--run-url", "https://ci/run/1",
+            "--expected-shards", "2",
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(rc, 1)
+        self.assertIn("gh-1658: 1 shard contributed 0 trials", out)
+        self.assertIn("do not paste", out)
+
+    def test_gpu_shard_index_is_guarded_too(self):
+        # The modal leg rides the same matrix (split_tasks numbers it
+        # after the CPU shards): a vanished GPU shard is equally named.
+        make_jobs(self.jobs, "fa-2.1-docker-cpu-0", [{"resolved": True}])
+        rc, out = self._run(str(self.jobs), "--family", "2.1", "--expected-shards", "2")
+        self.assertEqual(rc, 1)
+        self.assertIn("- shard 1: 0 trials", out)
+
+

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1664
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1664
- **Title**: gh-1658 [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry on zero-trial startup crash (shard-12 lost 6% of run 38823577512)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1658` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +487
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T07:36:55Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T12:09:24Z

## PR Description

Closes #1658
### What changed
- `Bench Harbor` shard step (`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`): when the harbor run fails with **zero** `result.json` files under the shard's job dir, the invocation is retried once inline (same env/model/params); a failure with ≥1 trial exits immediately — a real result, never retried.
- Aggregate guard: `bench/harbor_fa/summary.py` grows `--expected-shards N` (setup matrix length via `jq`), wired into the `Aggregate resolution rate` step — the verdict fails **by name** on any shard that contributed 0 trials to the merged export, with a do-not-paste caveat on the ledger row.
- `docs/bench.md`: new "Shard startup failures (gh-1658)" section — zero-trial retries once inline; a red shard with trials is a real result and is never auto-retried.

### Key decisions
- Retry gate keys on `result.json` **presence** under the shard job dir — the same presence rule the summary's completeness count uses.
- Attempt 1's trial-less dir is preserved under `jobs/_attempt1-<name>`: RCA evidence survives, and the name never matches the `fa-<family>-*` export globs, so the merged export / Hub upload cannot double-count.
- Still-failing zero-trial shard writes `zero-trial startup failure (retried once)` to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` — RCA no longer depends on job logs surviving.
- The harbor run block is pure shell (matrix identity rides step env `SHARD_KIND`/`SHARD_INDEX`), so `ZeroTrialRetryTest` **executes it verbatim** against a fake harbor: success = 1 invocation, no marker; zero-trial crash = exactly 1 retry with the same `--job-name`, proceeds on success; failure with trials = never retried.

### How to verify
```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa   # 211 tests OK — incl. 13 new gh-1658 tests (retry contract + shard guard)
actionlint .github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml     # no new findings (only the 2 pre-existing info-level shellcheck notes)
```
Post-merge manual smoke: dispatch `tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1` — the retry branch must be a no-op on success (no double trials).

Note: `bench/terminal_bench` has 1 pre-existing test-import error (`test_fa_usage`, harbor package mismatch on this runner) — reproduced on base `3464f84`, untouched here.

====
# gh-1658: [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry on zero-trial startup crash (shard-12 lost 6% of run 38823577512)

## Description

## [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry when a shard crashes at startup with zero trials

### Product frame

A shard job that dies before its first trial is pure infra loss — it silently deletes ~6% of a full run's capacity and (if unnoticed) corrupts the aggregate. Run 38823577512 lost shard 12 this way: the "Run harbor" step failed after 12 s with zero trials started (docker/rate-limit/dataset-resolve transient — root cause unprovable, job log was lost to the rerun). Attempt 2 of the same shard ran fine (11/25). A transient startup crash must not cost a shard.

### Required capabilities

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1664
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1664
- **Title**: gh-1658 [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry on zero-trial startup crash (shard-12 lost 6% of run 38823577512)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1658` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +487
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T07:36:55Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T12:09:24Z

## PR Description

Closes #1658
### What changed
- `Bench Harbor` shard step (`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`): when the harbor run fails with **zero** `result.json` files under the shard's job dir, the invocation is retried once inline (same env/model/params); a failure with ≥1 trial exits immediately — a real result, never retried.
- Aggregate guard: `bench/harbor_fa/summary.py` grows `--expected-shards N` (setup matrix length via `jq`), wired into the `Aggregate resolution rate` step — the verdict fails **by name** on any shard that contributed 0 trials to the merged export, with a do-not-paste caveat on the ledger row.
- `docs/bench.md`: new "Shard startup failures (gh-1658)" section — zero-trial retries once inline; a red shard with trials is a real result and is never auto-retried.

### Key decisions
- Retry gate keys on `result.json` **presence** under the shard job dir — the same presence rule the summary's completeness count uses.
- Attempt 1's trial-less dir is preserved under `jobs/_attempt1-<name>`: RCA evidence survives, and the name never matches the `fa-<family>-*` export globs, so the merged export / Hub upload cannot double-count.
- Still-failing zero-trial shard writes `zero-trial startup failure (retried once)` to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` — RCA no longer depends on job logs surviving.
- The harbor run block is pure shell (matrix identity rides step env `SHARD_KIND`/`SHARD_INDEX`), so `ZeroTrialRetryTest` **executes it verbatim** against a fake harbor: success = 1 invocation, no marker; zero-trial crash = exactly 1 retry with the same `--job-name`, proceeds on success; failure with trials = never retried.

### How to verify
```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa   # 211 tests OK — incl. 13 new gh-1658 tests (retry contract + shard guard)
actionlint .github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml     # no new findings (only the 2 pre-existing info-level shellcheck notes)
```
Post-merge manual smoke: dispatch `tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1` — the retry branch must be a no-op on success (no double trials).

Note: `bench/terminal_bench` has 1 pre-existing test-import error (`test_fa_usage`, harbor package mismatch on this runner) — reproduced on base `3464f84`, untouched here.

# gh-1658: [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry on zero-trial startup crash (shard-12 lost 6% of run 38823577512)

## Description

## [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry when a shard crashes at startup with zero trials

### Product frame

A shard job that dies before its first trial is pure infra loss — it silently deletes ~6% of a full run's capacity and (if unnoticed) corrupts the aggregate. Run 38823577512 lost shard 12 this way: the "Run harbor" step failed after 12 s with zero trials started (docker/rate-limit/dataset-resolve transient — root cause unprovable, job log was lost to the rerun). Attempt 2 of the same shard ran fine (11/25). A transient startup crash must not cost a shard.

### Required capabilities

- **C1 — inline retry, zero-trial only.** In `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`, the shard job's harbor step: when the harbor run fails AND the shard's trial dir contains 0 `result.json` files, retry the harbor invocation once (same env/model/params). A failure WITH trials is a real result — never retried (it would double-bill and mix attempts).
- **C2 — explicit marker.** On a still-failing zero-trial shard, the step summary states `zero-trial startup failure (retried once)` so the RCA does not depend on job logs surviving.
- **C3 — aggregate guard.** The "Aggregate resolution rate" job fails loudly if any shard contributes 0 trials to the merged export (a shard that vanished from artifacts must not silently shrink the denominator).
- **C4 — docs.** `docs/bench.md` gets two lines: zero-trial retries once inline; a red shard with trials is a real result and is never auto-retried.

### Test matrix

- Workflow YAML lint / actionlint in CI (existing gates).
- Manual smoke: dispatch `tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1` and verify the retry branch is a no-op on success (no double trials in the export).
- The C3 aggregate guard is exercised by the existing summary scripts' empty-shard path (add a fixture if the merge script has none).

### Platform inventory

- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` (shard job harbor step + aggregate job).
- `docs/bench.md`.
- No Dart changes, no harness changes.

### Security

No new secrets, no new network paths; same container invocation retried.

### Acceptance

- [ ] AC1: a zero-trial startup failure retries once inside the same job and proceeds on success.
- [ ] AC2: a failure with ≥1 trial is never retried.
- [ ] AC3: aggregate job fails on any zero-trial shard.
- [ ] AC4: next full run loses no shard capacity to a startup transient without a visible retried-once marker.

          FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION: '1'
          FA_STALL_GAP_SEC: '360'
          FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC: '3600'
          # gh-1576: the shard's external harness cap — the MIN of the
          # dataset-declared per-task agent timeouts (task.toml
          # `[agent] timeout_sec`, resolved pre-launch by split_tasks.py).
          # A shard where no task declares one emits NO key, which renders
          # as an empty env var = unknown: the knobs rule alone,
          # byte-identical (AC5, no invented clock — E1). When present,
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py folds it in via min() so fa's
          # deadline can never outlive harbor's per-task kill (I1) — the
          # adapter decides the kill at the cap and the audit names it
          # (outcome `external_cap`); a kill that still comes from
          # outside (harbor's wait_for / SIGTERM) flushes outcome
          # `external_kill` (I2).
          FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC: ${{ matrix.external_cap }}
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
          # gh-1658 C1: the matrix identity rides the step env so the run
          # block stays pure shell — the retry REG
          # (test_bench_harbor_workflow.py::ZeroTrialRetryTest) executes
          # the block verbatim in a subprocess, where `${{ }}` would be a
          # bash bad substitution.
          SHARD_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD_INDEX: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1503 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).
          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"
          args=()
          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-i "$t"); done
          # Issue #1122 knobs, same env contract as bench.yml (shared
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py). gh-1556 AC2: the watch knobs now
          # ride the step env block on every shard (progress-watch is the
          # bench default), so the adapter always supervises — only
          # removing those exports restores the unsupervised run. The
          # inputs below stay meaningful ON TOP of the watch defaults:
          # an explicit agent-timeout clips the watch ceiling to base x4
          # (the pre-PR ladder semantics — under the watch the abs
          # ceiling is the cap that actually kills a progressing trial),
          # and an explicit progress-extension: false unsets the
          # step-env extension. With both inputs empty the step-env
          # watch values rule unchanged.
          # A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
            # gh-1556 rework: without this clip an operator-set base cap
            # would be silently ignored — under watch+extension the abs
            # ceiling alone bounds a progressing trial (base_sec is only
            # consulted with the extension off).
            # The watch exports are individually removable (the escape
            # hatch back to the legacy ladder): if the ceiling export
            # alone is gone, default it to base x4 under `set -u`
            # (exactly what the legacy ladder would have used) before
            # the clip — an unbound variable must not kill the shard.
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
          fi
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            ''|0|1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on|false|FALSE|False|no|off) ;;
            *) echo "::error::progress-extension must be boolean (true/false), got '$PROGRESS_EXTENSION'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            # gh-1556 rework: the step env exports FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1
            # (the watch default) — an explicit false must still win by
            # unsetting it, otherwise the input is a silent no-op.
            false|FALSE|False|no|off) unset FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION;;
            1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on) export FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1;;

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # harbor exits 0 even with unresolved trials; the verdict here covers
      # run completeness — every expected trial attempted — after the merged
      # artifact below is uploaded.
      - name: Upload merged harbor jobs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: harbor-jobs-merged
          path: jobs/

      - name: Resolution summary & verdict
        if: always()
        env:
          EXPECTED_TASKS: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.count }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
          # gh-1503: pinned to the setup resolve step's outputs — the
          # free-text model input is gone; provider+model is derived
          # from the provider choice (same contract as bench.yml).
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          # gh-1503: the report names the provider+model — glm and kimi
          # runs never blend in the ledger/cost views.
          BENCH_RUN_LABEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          # gh-1658 C3: the shard count the run fielded (the setup split's
          # matrix) — the aggregate fails by name on any shard that
          # contributed 0 trials to the merged export.
          MATRIX_JSON: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.matrix }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          expected_trials=$((EXPECTED_TASKS * ATTEMPTS))
          # gh-1658 C3: the expected shard set is derived from the setup
          # split (never hardcoded) — summary.py fails the verdict when a
          # shard index carries no trial in the merged export.
          expected_shards=$(printf '%s' "$MATRIX_JSON" | jq '.include | length')
          python bench/harbor_fa/summary.py --family "$FAMILY" \
            --model "$MODEL" --fa-ref "$FA_REF" --run-url "$RUN_URL" \
            --expected-trials "$expected_trials" \
            --expected-shards "$expected_shards" jobs

## PR Description

Closes #1658
### What changed
- `Bench Harbor` shard step (`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`): when the harbor run fails with **zero** `result.json` files under the shard's job dir, the invocation is retried once inline (same env/model/params); a failure with ≥1 trial exits immediately — a real result, never retried.
- Aggregate guard: `bench/harbor_fa/summary.py` grows `--expected-shards N` (setup matrix length via `jq`), wired into the `Aggregate resolution rate` step — the verdict fails **by name** on any shard that contributed 0 trials to the merged export, with a do-not-paste caveat on the ledger row.
- `docs/bench.md`: new "Shard startup failures (gh-1658)" section — zero-trial retries once inline; a red shard with trials is a real result and is never auto-retried.

### Key decisions
- Retry gate keys on `result.json` **presence** under the shard job dir — the same presence rule the summary's completeness count uses.
- Attempt 1's trial-less dir is preserved under `jobs/_attempt1-<name>`: RCA evidence survives, and the name never matches the `fa-<family>-*` export globs, so the merged export / Hub upload cannot double-count.
- Still-failing zero-trial shard writes `zero-trial startup failure (retried once)` to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` — RCA no longer depends on job logs surviving.

```bash
actionlint .github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml     # no new findings (only the 2 pre-existing info-level shellcheck notes)
```

# gh-1658: [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry on zero-trial startup crash (shard-12 lost 6% of run 38823577512)

## Description

## [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry when a shard crashes at startup with zero trials

### Product frame

A shard job that dies before its first trial is pure infra loss — it silently deletes ~6% of a full run's capacity and (if unnoticed) corrupts the aggregate. Run 38823577512 lost shard 12 this way: the "Run harbor" step failed after 12 s with zero trials started (docker/rate-limit/dataset-resolve transient — root cause unprovable, job log was lost to the rerun). Attempt 2 of the same shard ran fine (11/25). A transient startup crash must not cost a shard.

### Required capabilities

- **C1 — inline retry, zero-trial only.** In `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`, the shard job's harbor step: when the harbor run fails AND the shard's trial dir contains 0 `result.json` files, retry the harbor invocation once (same env/model/params). A failure WITH trials is a real result — never retried (it would double-bill and mix attempts).
- **C2 — explicit marker.** On a still-failing zero-trial shard, the step summary states `zero-trial startup failure (retried once)` so the RCA does not depend on job logs surviving.
- **C3 — aggregate guard.** The "Aggregate resolution rate" job fails loudly if any shard contributes 0 trials to the merged export (a shard that vanished from artifacts must not silently shrink the denominator).
- **C4 — docs.** `docs/bench.md` gets two lines: zero-trial retries once inline; a red shard with trials is a real result and is never auto-retried.

### Test matrix

- Workflow YAML lint / actionlint in CI (existing gates).
- Manual smoke: dispatch `tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1` and verify the retry branch is a no-op on success (no double trials in the export).
- The C3 aggregate guard is exercised by the existing summary scripts' empty-shard path (add a fixture if the merge script has none).

### Platform inventory

- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` (shard job harbor step + aggregate job).
- `docs/bench.md`.
- No Dart changes, no harness changes.

### Security

No new secrets, no new network paths; same container invocation retried.

### Acceptance

- [ ] AC1: a zero-trial startup failure retries once inside the same job and proceeds on success.
- [ ] AC2: a failure with ≥1 trial is never retried.
- [ ] AC3: aggregate job fails on any zero-trial shard.
- [ ] AC4: next full run loses no shard capacity to a startup transient without a visible retried-once marker.

          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
          # gh-1658 C1: the matrix identity rides the step env so the run
          # block stays pure shell — the retry REG
          # (test_bench_harbor_workflow.py::ZeroTrialRetryTest) executes
          # the block verbatim in a subprocess, where `${{ }}` would be a
          # bash bad substitution.
          SHARD_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD_INDEX: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1503 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).
          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"
          args=()
          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-i "$t"); done
          # Issue #1122 knobs, same env contract as bench.yml (shared
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py). gh-1556 AC2: the watch knobs now
          # ride the step env block on every shard (progress-watch is the
          # bench default), so the adapter always supervises — only
          # removing those exports restores the unsupervised run. The
          # inputs below stay meaningful ON TOP of the watch defaults:
          # an explicit agent-timeout clips the watch ceiling to base x4
          # (the pre-PR ladder semantics — under the watch the abs
          # ceiling is the cap that actually kills a progressing trial),
          # and an explicit progress-extension: false unsets the
          # step-env extension. With both inputs empty the step-env
          # watch values rule unchanged.
          # A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
            # gh-1556 rework: without this clip an operator-set base cap
            # would be silently ignored — under watch+extension the abs
            # ceiling alone bounds a progressing trial (base_sec is only
            # consulted with the extension off).
            # The watch exports are individually removable (the escape
            # hatch back to the legacy ladder): if the ceiling export
            # alone is gone, default it to base x4 under `set -u`
            # (exactly what the legacy ladder would have used) before
            # the clip — an unbound variable must not kill the shard.
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
          fi
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            ''|0|1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on|false|FALSE|False|no|off) ;;
            *) echo "::error::progress-extension must be boolean (true/false), got '$PROGRESS_EXTENSION'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            # gh-1556 rework: the step env exports FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1
            # (the watch default) — an explicit false must still win by
            # unsetting it, otherwise the input is a silent no-op.
            false|FALSE|False|no|off) unset FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION;;
            1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on) export FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1;;
          esac
          # gh-1658 C1: the harbor invocation + the zero-trial inline
          # retry. The job name stays pinned (one jobs/<name>/ dir per
          # shard, so the summary job's downloads cannot collide on
          # harbor's timestamped default; the family label keys results
          # per dataset version — fa-4.0-* matches the historical 4.0
          # names exactly) and is built from step-env matrix values so
          # the whole block remains pure shell.
          JOB_NAME="fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${SHARD_KIND}-${SHARD_INDEX}"
          run_harbor() {
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent \
              -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" \
              --job-name "$JOB_NAME" -o jobs \
              "${args[@]}"
          }
          # The zero-trial gate counts result.json PRESENCE anywhere
          # under the shard's job dir — the same presence rule the
          # summary's completeness count uses.
          trials_started() {
            [ -d "jobs/$JOB_NAME" ] || { echo 0; return 0; }
            find "jobs/$JOB_NAME" -name result.json | wc -l
          }
          if run_harbor; then
            :
          else
            harbor_status=$?
            if [ "$(trials_started)" -gt 0 ]; then
              # gh-1658 C1/AC2: a failure WITH trials is a real result —
              # never retried (a retry would double-bill and mix attempts).
              exit "$harbor_status"
            fi
            # gh-1658 C1/AC1: zero trials = a startup crash (docker /
            # rate-limit / dataset-resolve transient). Retry ONCE with
            # the same env/model/params; attempt 1's trial-less dir moves
            # aside so the retry owns the pinned job name and the failed
            # attempt's logs survive for RCA. The preserved dir never
            # matches the fa-<family>-* export globs (Hub upload +
            # summary family filter), so the merged export cannot
            # double-count its trials.
            mv "jobs/$JOB_NAME" "jobs/_attempt1-$JOB_NAME" 2>/dev/null || true
            if run_harbor; then
              echo "::warning::shard $JOB_NAME: zero-trial startup crash recovered by the inline retry (attempt 1 kept under jobs/_attempt1-$JOB_NAME)"
            else
              # gh-1658 C2: the marker keeps the RCA independent of job
              # logs surviving the rerun.
              {
                echo "## Shard $JOB_NAME"
                echo
                echo "zero-trial startup failure (retried once)"
              } >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/null}"
              exit 1
            fi
          fi

        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2

with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned: the adapter targets the 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent contract.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

      # Same gate as bench.yml: stdlib-only bench script tests. Two
      # discovery roots: bench/terminal_bench (legacy scripts + the
      # harbor parity suite from #1122 — terminal-bench is installed
      # just for the legacy-adapter import surface) and bench/harbor_fa
      # (the #1124 family/summary suites + the #1123 token/cost summary
      # tests). Discovering bench/ itself would need __init__.py
      # plumbing the bench dirs don't have.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          pip install 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v

      # Download the dataset once for classification; harbor re-fetches
      # into its own cache during the run. DATASET is the canonical id
      # resolved by the family step (the raw input may be a bare label).
      - name: Shard dataset into CPU / GPU shards
        id: shards
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          SHARDS: ${{ inputs.shards }}
          CPU_ENV: ${{ inputs.cpu-env }}
        run: |
          harbor datasets download "$DATASET" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds" --overwrite
          # Dataset name at version: dir name is the dataset slug.
          ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds/$(basename "${DATASET%%@*}")"
          [ -d "$ds_dir" ] || ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds"
          # split_tasks.py writes the matrix/counts into GITHUB_OUTPUT itself.
          # harbor -i matches qualified ids (<org>/<name>): prefix with the
          # org part of the dataset spec.
          python bench/harbor_fa/split_tasks.py "$ds_dir" \
            --filter "$TASKS" --shards "$SHARDS" --cpu-env "$CPU_ENV" \
            --task-prefix "${DATASET%%/*}/"

  bench:
    name: fa on tbench ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}, shard ${{ matrix.i }} (${{ matrix.env }}, ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }})
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.cpu-runner }}
    # ~4 tasks/shard x --n-attempts x task runtime (tbench agent caps
===
      - name: Upload harbor job (shard ${{ matrix.i }})
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: harbor-job-shard-${{ matrix.i }}
          path: jobs/

      - name: Upload to Harbor Hub
        if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''
        env:
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          for job_dir in jobs/fa-${FAMILY}-*; do
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor upload "$job_dir" --public
          done

  summary:
    name: Aggregate resolution rate
    needs: [setup, bench]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download shard results
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: harbor-job-shard-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: jobs

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # harbor exits 0 even with unresolved trials; the verdict here covers
      # run completeness — every expected trial attempted — after the merged
      # artifact below is uploaded.
      - name: Upload merged harbor jobs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: harbor-jobs-merged
          path: jobs/

      - name: Resolution summary & verdict
        if: always()
        env:
          EXPECTED_TASKS: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.count }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
          # gh-1503: pinned to the setup resolve step's outputs — the
          # free-text model input is gone; provider+model is derived
          # from the provider choice (same contract as bench.yml).
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          # gh-1503: the report names the provider+model — glm and kimi
          # runs never blend in the ledger/cost views.
          BENCH_RUN_LABEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          # gh-1658 C3: the shard count the run fielded (the setup split's
          # matrix) — the aggregate fails by name on any shard that
          # contributed 0 trials to the merged export.
          MATRIX_JSON: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.matrix }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          expected_trials=$((EXPECTED_TASKS * ATTEMPTS))
          # gh-1658 C3: the expected shard set is derived from the setup
          # split (never hardcoded) — summary.py fails the verdict when a
          # shard index carries no trial in the merged export.
          expected_shards=$(printf '%s' "$MATRIX_JSON" | jq '.include | length')
          python bench/harbor_fa/summary.py --family "$FAMILY" \
            --model "$MODEL" --fa-ref "$FA_REF" --run-url "$RUN_URL" \
            --expected-trials "$expected_trials" \
            --expected-shards "$expected_shards" jobs

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1664
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1664
- **Title**: gh-1658 [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry on zero-trial startup crash (shard-12 lost 6% of run 38823577512)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1658` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +487
- **Deletions**: -11
- **Created**: 2026-10-17T07:36:55Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-17T12:09:24Z

## PR Description

Closes #1658
### What changed
- `Bench Harbor` shard step (`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`): when the harbor run fails with **zero** `result.json` files under the shard's job dir, the invocation is retried once inline (same env/model/params); a failure with ≥1 trial exits immediately — a real result, never retried.
- Aggregate guard: `bench/harbor_fa/summary.py` grows `--expected-shards N` (setup matrix length via `jq`), wired into the `Aggregate resolution rate` step — the verdict fails **by name** on any shard that contributed 0 trials to the merged export, with a do-not-paste caveat on the ledger row.
- `docs/bench.md`: new "Shard startup failures (gh-1658)" section — zero-trial retries once inline; a red shard with trials is a real result and is never auto-retried.

### Key decisions
- Retry gate keys on `result.json` **presence** under the shard job dir — the same presence rule the summary's completeness count uses.
- Attempt 1's trial-less dir is preserved under `jobs/_attempt1-<name>`: RCA evidence survives, and the name never matches the `fa-<family>-*` export globs, so the merged export / Hub upload cannot double-count.
- Still-failing zero-trial shard writes `zero-trial startup failure (retried once)` to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` — RCA no longer depends on job logs surviving.

# gh-1658: [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry on zero-trial startup crash (shard-12 lost 6% of run 38823577512)

## Description

## [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry when a shard crashes at startup with zero trials

### Product frame

A shard job that dies before its first trial is pure infra loss — it silently deletes ~6% of a full run's capacity and (if unnoticed) corrupts the aggregate. Run 38823577512 lost shard 12 this way: the "Run harbor" step failed after 12 s with zero trials started (docker/rate-limit/dataset-resolve transient — root cause unprovable, job log was lost to the rerun). Attempt 2 of the same shard ran fine (11/25). A transient startup crash must not cost a shard.

### Required capabilities

- **C1 — inline retry, zero-trial only.** In `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`, the shard job's harbor step: when the harbor run fails AND the shard's trial dir contains 0 `result.json` files, retry the harbor invocation once (same env/model/params). A failure WITH trials is a real result — never retried (it would double-bill and mix attempts).
- **C2 — explicit marker.** On a still-failing zero-trial shard, the step summary states `zero-trial startup failure (retried once)` so the RCA does not depend on job logs surviving.
- **C3 — aggregate guard.** The "Aggregate resolution rate" job fails loudly if any shard contributes 0 trials to the merged export (a shard that vanished from artifacts must not silently shrink the denominator).
- **C4 — docs.** `docs/bench.md` gets two lines: zero-trial retries once inline; a red shard with trials is a real result and is never auto-retried.

### Test matrix

- Workflow YAML lint / actionlint in CI (existing gates).
- Manual smoke: dispatch `tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1` and verify the retry branch is a no-op on success (no double trials in the export).
- The C3 aggregate guard is exercised by the existing summary scripts' empty-shard path (add a fixture if the merge script has none).

### Platform inventory

- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` (shard job harbor step + aggregate job).
- `docs/bench.md`.
- No Dart changes, no harness changes.

### Security

No new secrets, no new network paths; same container invocation retried.

### Acceptance

- [ ] AC1: a zero-trial startup failure retries once inside the same job and proceeds on success.
- [ ] AC2: a failure with ≥1 trial is never retried.
- [ ] AC3: aggregate job fails on any zero-trial shard.
- [ ] AC4: next full run loses no shard capacity to a startup transient without a visible retried-once marker.

# only arms its gap-aware decision under the extension).
          FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION: '1'
          FA_STALL_GAP_SEC: '360'
          FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC: '3600'
          # gh-1576: the shard's external harness cap — the MIN of the
          # dataset-declared per-task agent timeouts (task.toml
          # `[agent] timeout_sec`, resolved pre-launch by split_tasks.py).
          # A shard where no task declares one emits NO key, which renders
          # as an empty env var = unknown: the knobs rule alone,
          # byte-identical (AC5, no invented clock — E1). When present,
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py folds it in via min() so fa's
          # deadline can never outlive harbor's per-task kill (I1) — the
          # adapter decides the kill at the cap and the audit names it
          # (outcome `external_cap`); a kill that still comes from
          # outside (harbor's wait_for / SIGTERM) flushes outcome
          # `external_kill` (I2).
          FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC: ${{ matrix.external_cap }}
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
          # gh-1658 C1: the matrix identity rides the step env so the run
          # block stays pure shell — the retry REG
          # (test_bench_harbor_workflow.py::ZeroTrialRetryTest) executes
          # the block verbatim in a subprocess, where `${{ }}` would be a
          # bash bad substitution.
          SHARD_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD_INDEX: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1503 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).
          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"
          args=()
          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-i "$t"); done
          # Issue #1122 knobs, same env contract as bench.yml (shared
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py). gh-1556 AC2: the watch knobs now
          # ride the step env block on every shard (progress-watch is the
          # bench default), so the adapter always supervises — only
          # removing those exports restores the unsupervised run. The
          # inputs below stay meaningful ON TOP of the watch defaults:
          # an explicit agent-timeout clips the watch ceiling to base x4
          # (the pre-PR ladder semantics — under the watch the abs
          # ceiling is the cap that actually kills a progressing trial),
          # and an explicit progress-extension: false unsets the
          # step-env extension. With both inputs empty the step-env
          # watch values rule unchanged.
          # A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
            # gh-1556 rework: without this clip an operator-set base cap
            # would be silently ignored — under watch+extension the abs
            # ceiling alone bounds a progressing trial (base_sec is only
            # consulted with the extension off).
            # The watch exports are individually removable (the escape
            # hatch back to the legacy ladder): if the ceiling export
            # alone is gone, default it to base x4 under `set -u`
            # (exactly what the legacy ladder would have used) before
            # the clip — an unbound variable must not kill the shard.
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
          fi
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            ''|0|1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on|false|FALSE|False|no|off) ;;
            *) echo "::error::progress-extension must be boolean (true/false), got '$PROGRESS_EXTENSION'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            # gh-1556 rework: the step env exports FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1
            # (the watch default) — an explicit false must still win by
            # unsetting it, otherwise the input is a silent no-op.
            false|FALSE|False|no|off) unset FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION;;
            1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on) export FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1;;
          esac
          # gh-1658 C1: the harbor invocation + the zero-trial inline
          # retry. The job name stays pinned (one jobs/<name>/ dir per
          # shard, so the summary job's downloads cannot collide on
          # harbor's timestamped default; the family label keys results
          # per dataset version — fa-4.0-* matches the historical 4.0
          # names exactly) and is built from step-env matrix values so
          # the whole block remains pure shell.
          JOB_NAME="fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${SHARD_KIND}-${SHARD_INDEX}"
          run_harbor() {
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent \
              -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" \
              --job-name "$JOB_NAME" -o jobs \
              "${args[@]}"
          }
          # The zero-trial gate counts result.json PRESENCE anywhere
          # under the shard's job dir — the same presence rule the
          # summary's completeness count uses.
          trials_started() {
            [ -d "jobs/$JOB_NAME" ] || { echo 0; return 0; }
            find "jobs/$JOB_NAME" -name result.json | wc -l
          }
          if run_harbor; then
            :
          else
            harbor_status=$?
            if [ "$(trials_started)" -gt 0 ]; then
              # gh-1658 C1/AC2: a failure WITH trials is a real result —
              # never retried (a retry would double-bill and mix attempts).
              exit "$harbor_status"
            fi
            # gh-1658 C1/AC1: zero trials = a startup crash (docker /
            # rate-limit / dataset-resolve transient). Retry ONCE with
            # the same env/model/params; attempt 1's trial-less dir moves
            # aside so the retry owns the pinned job name and the failed
            # attempt's logs survive for RCA. The preserved dir never
            # matches the fa-<family>-* export globs (Hub upload +
            # summary family filter), so the merged export cannot
            # double-count its trials.
            mv "jobs/$JOB_NAME" "jobs/_attempt1-$JOB_NAME" 2>/dev/null || true
            if run_harbor; then
              echo "::warning::shard $JOB_NAME: zero-trial startup crash recovered by the inline retry (attempt 1 kept under jobs/_attempt1-$JOB_NAME)"
            else
              # gh-1658 C2: the marker keeps the RCA independent of job
              # logs surviving the rerun.
              {
                echo "## Shard $JOB_NAME"
                echo
                echo "zero-trial startup failure (retried once)"
              } >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/null}"
              exit 1
            fi
          fi

with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned: the adapter targets the 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent contract.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

      # Same gate as bench.yml: stdlib-only bench script tests. Two
      # discovery roots: bench/terminal_bench (legacy scripts + the
      # harbor parity suite from #1122 — terminal-bench is installed
      # just for the legacy-adapter import surface) and bench/harbor_fa
      # (the #1124 family/summary suites + the #1123 token/cost summary
      # tests). Discovering bench/ itself would need __init__.py
      # plumbing the bench dirs don't have.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          pip install 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v

      # Download the dataset once for classification; harbor re-fetches
      # into its own cache during the run. DATASET is the canonical id
      # resolved by the family step (the raw input may be a bare label).
      - name: Shard dataset into CPU / GPU shards
        id: shards
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          SHARDS: ${{ inputs.shards }}
          CPU_ENV: ${{ inputs.cpu-env }}
        run: |
          harbor datasets download "$DATASET" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds" --overwrite
          # Dataset name at version: dir name is the dataset slug.
          ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds/$(basename "${DATASET%%@*}")"

          # split_tasks.py writes the matrix/counts into GITHUB_OUTPUT itself.
          # harbor -i matches qualified ids (<org>/<name>): prefix with the
          # org part of the dataset spec.

            --filter "$TASKS" --shards "$SHARDS" --cpu-env "$CPU_ENV" \

# gh-1658: [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry on zero-trial startup crash (shard-12 lost 6% of run 38823577512)

## Description

## [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry when a shard crashes at startup with zero trials

### Product frame

A shard job that dies before its first trial is pure infra loss — it silently deletes ~6% of a full run's capacity and (if unnoticed) corrupts the aggregate. Run 38823577512 lost shard 12 this way: the "Run harbor" step failed after 12 s with zero trials started (docker/rate-limit/dataset-resolve transient — root cause unprovable, job log was lost to the rerun). Attempt 2 of the same shard ran fine (11/25). A transient startup crash must not cost a shard.

### Required capabilities

- **C1 — inline retry, zero-trial only.** In `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`, the shard job's harbor step: when the harbor run fails AND the shard's trial dir contains 0 `result.json` files, retry the harbor invocation once (same env/model/params). A failure WITH trials is a real result — never retried (it would double-bill and mix attempts).
- **C2 — explicit marker.** On a still-failing zero-trial shard, the step summary states `zero-trial startup failure (retried once)` so the RCA does not depend on job logs surviving.
- **C3 — aggregate guard.** The "Aggregate resolution rate" job fails loudly if any shard contributes 0 trials to the merged export (a shard that vanished from artifacts must not silently shrink the denominator).
- **C4 — docs.** `docs/bench.md` gets two lines: zero-trial retries once inline; a red shard with trials is a real result and is never auto-retried.

### Test matrix

- Workflow YAML lint / actionlint in CI (existing gates).
- Manual smoke: dispatch `tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1` and verify the retry branch is a no-op on success (no double trials in the export).
- The C3 aggregate guard is exercised by the existing summary scripts' empty-shard path (add a fixture if the merge script has none).

### Platform inventory

- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` (shard job harbor step + aggregate job).
- `docs/bench.md`.
- No Dart changes, no harness changes.

### Security

No new secrets, no new network paths; same container invocation retried.

### Acceptance

- [ ] AC1: a zero-trial startup failure retries once inside the same job and proceeds on success.
- [ ] AC2: a failure with ≥1 trial is never retried.
- [ ] AC3: aggregate job fails on any zero-trial shard.
- [ ] AC4: next full run loses no shard capacity to a startup transient without a visible retried-once marker.

# only arms its gap-aware decision under the extension).
          FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION: '1'
          FA_STALL_GAP_SEC: '360'
          FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC: '3600'
          # gh-1576: the shard's external harness cap — the MIN of the
          # dataset-declared per-task agent timeouts (task.toml
          # `[agent] timeout_sec`, resolved pre-launch by split_tasks.py).
          # A shard where no task declares one emits NO key, which renders
          # as an empty env var = unknown: the knobs rule alone,
          # byte-identical (AC5, no invented clock — E1). When present,
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py folds it in via min() so fa's
          # deadline can never outlive harbor's per-task kill (I1) — the
          # adapter decides the kill at the cap and the audit names it
          # (outcome `external_cap`); a kill that still comes from
          # outside (harbor's wait_for / SIGTERM) flushes outcome
          # `external_kill` (I2).
          FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC: ${{ matrix.external_cap }}
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
          # gh-1658 C1: the matrix identity rides the step env so the run
          # block stays pure shell — the retry REG
          # (test_bench_harbor_workflow.py::ZeroTrialRetryTest) executes
          # the block verbatim in a subprocess, where `${{ }}` would be a
          # bash bad substitution.
          SHARD_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD_INDEX: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1503 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).
          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"
          args=()
          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-i "$t"); done
          # Issue #1122 knobs, same env contract as bench.yml (shared
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py). gh-1556 AC2: the watch knobs now
          # ride the step env block on every shard (progress-watch is the
          # bench default), so the adapter always supervises — only
          # removing those exports restores the unsupervised run. The
          # inputs below stay meaningful ON TOP of the watch defaults:
          # an explicit agent-timeout clips the watch ceiling to base x4
          # (the pre-PR ladder semantics — under the watch the abs
          # ceiling is the cap that actually kills a progressing trial),
          # and an explicit progress-extension: false unsets the
          # step-env extension. With both inputs empty the step-env
          # watch values rule unchanged.
          # A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
            # gh-1556 rework: without this clip an operator-set base cap
            # would be silently ignored — under watch+extension the abs
            # ceiling alone bounds a progressing trial (base_sec is only
            # consulted with the extension off).
            # The watch exports are individually removable (the escape
            # hatch back to the legacy ladder): if the ceiling export
            # alone is gone, default it to base x4 under `set -u`
            # (exactly what the legacy ladder would have used) before
            # the clip — an unbound variable must not kill the shard.
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
          fi
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            ''|0|1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on|false|FALSE|False|no|off) ;;
            *) echo "::error::progress-extension must be boolean (true/false), got '$PROGRESS_EXTENSION'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            # gh-1556 rework: the step env exports FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1
            # (the watch default) — an explicit false must still win by
            # unsetting it, otherwise the input is a silent no-op.
            false|FALSE|False|no|off) unset FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION;;
            1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on) export FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1;;
          esac
          # gh-1658 C1: the harbor invocation + the zero-trial inline
          # retry. The job name stays pinned (one jobs/<name>/ dir per
          # shard, so the summary job's downloads cannot collide on
          # harbor's timestamped default; the family label keys results
          # per dataset version — fa-4.0-* matches the historical 4.0
          # names exactly) and is built from step-env matrix values so
          # the whole block remains pure shell.
          JOB_NAME="fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${SHARD_KIND}-${SHARD_INDEX}"
          run_harbor() {
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent \
              -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" \
              --job-name "$JOB_NAME" -o jobs \
              "${args[@]}"
          }
          # The zero-trial gate counts result.json PRESENCE anywhere
          # under the shard's job dir — the same presence rule the
          # summary's completeness count uses.
          trials_started() {
            [ -d "jobs/$JOB_NAME" ] || { echo 0; return 0; }
            find "jobs/$JOB_NAME" -name result.json | wc -l
          }
          if run_harbor; then
            :
          else
            harbor_status=$?
            if [ "$(trials_started)" -gt 0 ]; then
              # gh-1658 C1/AC2: a failure WITH trials is a real result —
              # never retried (a retry would double-bill and mix attempts).
              exit "$harbor_status"

            # gh-1658 C1/AC1: zero trials = a startup crash (docker /
            # rate-limit / dataset-resolve transient). Retry ONCE with
            # the same env/model/params; attempt 1's trial-less dir moves
            # aside so the retry owns the pinned job name and the failed
            # attempt's logs survive for RCA. The preserved dir never
            # matches the fa-<family>-* export globs (Hub upload +
            # summary family filter), so the merged export cannot
            # double-count its trials.
            mv "jobs/$JOB_NAME" "jobs/_attempt1-$JOB_NAME" 2>/dev/null || true
            if run_harbor; then
              echo "::warning::shard $JOB_NAME: zero-trial startup crash recovered by the inline retry (attempt 1 kept under jobs/_attempt1-$JOB_NAME)"
            else
              # gh-1658 C2: the marker keeps the RCA independent of job
              # logs surviving the rerun.
              {
                echo "## Shard $JOB_NAME"
                echo
                echo "zero-trial startup failure (retried once)"
              } >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/null}"
              exit 1
            fi
          fi

with:

      # Pinned: the adapter targets the 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent contract.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

      # Same gate as bench.yml: stdlib-only bench script tests. Two
      # discovery roots: bench/terminal_bench (legacy scripts + the
      # harbor parity suite from #1122 — terminal-bench is installed
      # just for the legacy-adapter import surface) and bench/harbor_fa
      # (the #1124 family/summary suites + the #1123 token/cost summary
      # tests). Discovering bench/ itself would need __init__.py
      # plumbing the bench dirs don't have.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          pip install 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v

      # Download the dataset once for classification; harbor re-fetches
      # into its own cache during the run. DATASET is the canonical id
      # resolved by the family step (the raw input may be a bare label).
      - name: Shard dataset into CPU / GPU shards
        id: shards
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          SHARDS: ${{ inputs.shards }}
          CPU_ENV: ${{ inputs.cpu-env }}
        run: |
          harbor datasets download "$DATASET" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds" --overwrite
          # Dataset name at version: dir name is the dataset slug.
          ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds/$(basename "${DATASET%%@*}")"
          [ -d "$ds_dir" ] || ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds"
          # split_tasks.py writes the matrix/counts into GITHUB_OUTPUT itself.
          # harbor -i matches qualified ids (<org>/<name>): prefix with the
          # org part of the dataset spec.
          python bench/harbor_fa/split_tasks.py "$ds_dir" \
            --filter "$TASKS" --shards "$SHARDS" --cpu-env "$CPU_ENV" \
            --task-prefix "${DATASET%%/*}/"

  bench:
    name: fa on tbench ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}, shard ${{ matrix.i }} (${{ matrix.env }}, ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }})
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.cpu-runner }}
    # ~4 tasks/shard x --n-attempts x task runtime (tbench agent caps

        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2

          name: harbor-job-shard-${{ matrix.i }}

        if: always() && env.HARBOR_API_KEY != ''
        env:
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          for job_dir in jobs/fa-${FAMILY}-*; do
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor upload "$job_dir" --public
          done

  summary:
    name: Aggregate resolution rate
    needs: [setup, bench]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download shard results
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: harbor-job-shard-*

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # harbor exits 0 even with unresolved trials; the verdict here covers
      # run completeness — every expected trial attempted — after the merged
      # artifact below is uploaded.
      - name: Upload merged harbor jobs
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: harbor-jobs-merged
          path: jobs/

      - name: Resolution summary & verdict
        if: always()
        env:
          EXPECTED_TASKS: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.count }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          FAMILY: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.family }}
          # gh-1503: pinned to the setup resolve step's outputs — the
          # free-text model input is gone; provider+model is derived
          # from the provider choice (same contract as bench.yml).
          MODEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.bench_model }}
          # gh-1503: the report names the provider+model — glm and kimi
          # runs never blend in the ledger/cost views.
          BENCH_RUN_LABEL: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.run_label }}
          FA_REF: ${{ github.sha }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          # gh-1658 C3: the shard count the run fielded (the setup split's
          # matrix) — the aggregate fails by name on any shard that
          # contributed 0 trials to the merged export.
          MATRIX_JSON: ${{ needs.setup.outputs.matrix }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          expected_trials=$((EXPECTED_TASKS * ATTEMPTS))
          # gh-1658 C3: the expected shard set is derived from the setup
          # split (never hardcoded) — summary.py fails the verdict when a
          # shard index carries no trial in the merged export.
          expected_shards=$(printf '%s' "$MATRIX_JSON" | jq '.include | length')
          python bench/harbor_fa/summary.py --family "$FAMILY" \
            --model "$MODEL" --fa-ref "$FA_REF" --run-url "$RUN_URL" \
            --expected-trials "$expected_trials" \
            --expected-shards "$expected_shards" jobs
