blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

Closes #1658

- `Bench Harbor` shard step (`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`): when the harbor run fails with **zero** `result.json` files under the shard's job dir, the invocation is retried once inline (same env/model/params); a failure with ≥1 trial exits immediately — a real result, never retried.

- Retry gate keys on `result.json` **presence** under the shard job dir — the same presence rule the summary's completeness count uses.

# gh-1658: [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry on zero-trial startup crash (shard-12 lost 6% of run 38823577512)

## Description

## [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry when a shard crashes at startup with zero trials

### Product frame

A shard job that dies before its first trial is pure infra loss — it silently deletes ~6% of a full run's capacity and (if unnoticed) corrupts the aggregate. Run 38823577512 lost shard 12 this way: the "Run harbor" step failed after 12 s with zero trials started (docker/rate-limit/dataset-resolve transient — root cause unprovable, job log was lost to the rerun). Attempt 2 of the same shard ran fine (11/25). A transient startup crash must not cost a shard.

### Required capabilities

- **C1 — inline retry, zero-trial only.** In `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`, the shard job's harbor step: when the harbor run fails AND the shard's trial dir contains 0 `result.json` files, retry the harbor invocation once (same env/model/params). A failure WITH trials is a real result — never retried (it would double-bill and mix attempts).
- **C2 — explicit marker.** On a still-failing zero-trial shard, the step summary states `zero-trial startup failure (retried once)` so the RCA does not depend on job logs surviving.
- **C3 — aggregate guard.** The "Aggregate resolution rate" job fails loudly if any shard contributes 0 trials to the merged export (a shard that vanished from artifacts must not silently shrink the denominator).
- **C4 — docs.** `docs/bench.md` gets two lines: zero-trial retries once inline; a red shard with trials is a real result and is never auto-retried.

### Test matrix

- Workflow YAML lint / actionlint in CI (existing gates).
- Manual smoke: dispatch `tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1` and verify the retry branch is a no-op on success (no double trials in the export).
- The C3 aggregate guard is exercised by the existing summary scripts' empty-shard path (add a fixture if the merge script has none).

### Platform inventory

- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` (shard job harbor step + aggregate job).
- `docs/bench.md`.
- No Dart changes, no harness changes.

### Security

No new secrets, no new network paths; same container invocation retried.

### Acceptance

- [ ] AC1: a zero-trial startup failure retries once inside the same job and proceeds on success.
- [ ] AC2: a failure with ≥1 trial is never retried.
- [ ] AC3: aggregate job fails on any zero-trial shard.
- [ ] AC4: next full run loses no shard capacity to a startup transient without a visible retried-once marker.

# only arms its gap-aware decision under the extension).
          FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION: '1'
          FA_STALL_GAP_SEC: '360'
          FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC: '3600'
          # gh-1576: the shard's external harness cap — the MIN of the
          # dataset-declared per-task agent timeouts (task.toml
          # `[agent] timeout_sec`, resolved pre-launch by split_tasks.py).
          # A shard where no task declares one emits NO key, which renders
          # as an empty env var = unknown: the knobs rule alone,
          # byte-identical (AC5, no invented clock — E1). When present,
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py folds it in via min() so fa's
          # deadline can never outlive harbor's per-task kill (I1) — the
          # adapter decides the kill at the cap and the audit names it
          # (outcome `external_cap`); a kill that still comes from
          # outside (harbor's wait_for / SIGTERM) flushes outcome
          # `external_kill` (I2).
          FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC: ${{ matrix.external_cap }}
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
          # gh-1658 C1: the matrix identity rides the step env so the run
          # block stays pure shell — the retry REG
          # (test_bench_harbor_workflow.py::ZeroTrialRetryTest) executes
          # the block verbatim in a subprocess, where `${{ }}` would be a
          # bash bad substitution.
          SHARD_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD_INDEX: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1503 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).
          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"
          args=()
          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-i "$t"); done
          # Issue #1122 knobs, same env contract as bench.yml (shared
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py). gh-1556 AC2: the watch knobs now
          # ride the step env block on every shard (progress-watch is the
          # bench default), so the adapter always supervises — only
          # removing those exports restores the unsupervised run. The
          # inputs below stay meaningful ON TOP of the watch defaults:
          # an explicit agent-timeout clips the watch ceiling to base x4
          # (the pre-PR ladder semantics — under the watch the abs
          # ceiling is the cap that actually kills a progressing trial),
          # and an explicit progress-extension: false unsets the
          # step-env extension. With both inputs empty the step-env
          # watch values rule unchanged.
          # A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
            # gh-1556 rework: without this clip an operator-set base cap
            # would be silently ignored — under watch+extension the abs
            # ceiling alone bounds a progressing trial (base_sec is only
            # consulted with the extension off).
            # The watch exports are individually removable (the escape
            # hatch back to the legacy ladder): if the ceiling export
            # alone is gone, default it to base x4 under `set -u`
            # (exactly what the legacy ladder would have used) before
            # the clip — an unbound variable must not kill the shard.
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
          fi
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            ''|0|1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on|false|FALSE|False|no|off) ;;
            *) echo "::error::progress-extension must be boolean (true/false), got '$PROGRESS_EXTENSION'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            # gh-1556 rework: the step env exports FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1
            # (the watch default) — an explicit false must still win by
            # unsetting it, otherwise the input is a silent no-op.
            false|FALSE|False|no|off) unset FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION;;
            1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on) export FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1;;
          esac
          # gh-1658 C1: the harbor invocation + the zero-trial inline
          # retry. The job name stays pinned (one jobs/<name>/ dir per
          # shard, so the summary job's downloads cannot collide on
          # harbor's timestamped default; the family label keys results
          # per dataset version — fa-4.0-* matches the historical 4.0
          # names exactly) and is built from step-env matrix values so
          # the whole block remains pure shell.
          JOB_NAME="fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${SHARD_KIND}-${SHARD_INDEX}"
          run_harbor() {
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent \
              -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" \
              --job-name "$JOB_NAME" -o jobs \
              "${args[@]}"
          }
          # The zero-trial gate counts result.json PRESENCE anywhere
          # under the shard's job dir — the same presence rule the
          # summary's completeness count uses.
          trials_started() {
            [ -d "jobs/$JOB_NAME" ] || { echo 0; return 0; }
            find "jobs/$JOB_NAME" -name result.json | wc -l

            :

              # gh-1658 C1/AC2: a failure WITH trials is a real result —
              # never retried (a retry would double-bill and mix attempts).
              exit "$harbor_status"

            # rate-limit / dataset-resolve transient). Retry ONCE with
            # the same env/model/params; attempt 1's trial-less dir moves
            # aside so the retry owns the pinned job name and the failed
            # attempt's logs survive for RCA. The preserved dir never
            # matches the fa-<family>-* export globs (Hub upload +
            # summary family filter), so the merged export cannot
            # double-count its trials.
            mv "jobs/$JOB_NAME" "jobs/_attempt1-$JOB_NAME" 2>/dev/null || true
            if run_harbor; then
              echo "::warning::shard $JOB_NAME: zero-trial startup crash recovered by the inline retry (attempt 1 kept under jobs/_attempt1-$JOB_NAME)"
            else
              # gh-1658 C2: the marker keeps the RCA independent of job
              # logs surviving the rerun.

                echo "## Shard $JOB_NAME"
                echo
                echo "zero-trial startup failure (retried once)"
              } >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/null}"
              exit 1
            fi

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),

# gh-1658: [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry on zero-trial startup crash (shard-12 lost 6% of run 38823577512)

## Description

## [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry when a shard crashes at startup with zero trials

### Product frame

A shard job that dies before its first trial is pure infra loss — it silently deletes ~6% of a full run's capacity and (if unnoticed) corrupts the aggregate. Run 38823577512 lost shard 12 this way: the "Run harbor" step failed after 12 s with zero trials started (docker/rate-limit/dataset-resolve transient — root cause unprovable, job log was lost to the rerun). Attempt 2 of the same shard ran fine (11/25). A transient startup crash must not cost a shard.

### Required capabilities

- **C1 — inline retry, zero-trial only.** In `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`, the shard job's harbor step: when the harbor run fails AND the shard's trial dir contains 0 `result.json` files, retry the harbor invocation once (same env/model/params). A failure WITH trials is a real result — never retried (it would double-bill and mix attempts).
- **C2 — explicit marker.** On a still-failing zero-trial shard, the step summary states `zero-trial startup failure (retried once)` so the RCA does not depend on job logs surviving.
- **C3 — aggregate guard.** The "Aggregate resolution rate" job fails loudly if any shard contributes 0 trials to the merged export (a shard that vanished from artifacts must not silently shrink the denominator).
- **C4 — docs.** `docs/bench.md` gets two lines: zero-trial retries once inline; a red shard with trials is a real result and is never auto-retried.

### Test matrix

- Workflow YAML lint / actionlint in CI (existing gates).
- Manual smoke: dispatch `tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1` and verify the retry branch is a no-op on success (no double trials in the export).
- The C3 aggregate guard is exercised by the existing summary scripts' empty-shard path (add a fixture if the merge script has none).

### Platform inventory

- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` (shard job harbor step + aggregate job).
- `docs/bench.md`.
- No Dart changes, no harness changes.

### Security

No new secrets, no new network paths; same container invocation retried.

### Acceptance

- [ ] AC1: a zero-trial startup failure retries once inside the same job and proceeds on success.
- [ ] AC2: a failure with ≥1 trial is never retried.
- [ ] AC3: aggregate job fails on any zero-trial shard.
- [ ] AC4: next full run loses no shard capacity to a startup transient without a visible retried-once marker.

# only arms its gap-aware decision under the extension).
          FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION: '1'
          FA_STALL_GAP_SEC: '360'
          FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC: '3600'
          # gh-1576: the shard's external harness cap — the MIN of the
          # dataset-declared per-task agent timeouts (task.toml
          # `[agent] timeout_sec`, resolved pre-launch by split_tasks.py).
          # A shard where no task declares one emits NO key, which renders
          # as an empty env var = unknown: the knobs rule alone,
          # byte-identical (AC5, no invented clock — E1). When present,
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py folds it in via min() so fa's
          # deadline can never outlive harbor's per-task kill (I1) — the
          # adapter decides the kill at the cap and the audit names it
          # (outcome `external_cap`); a kill that still comes from
          # outside (harbor's wait_for / SIGTERM) flushes outcome
          # `external_kill` (I2).
          FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC: ${{ matrix.external_cap }}
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
          # gh-1658 C1: the matrix identity rides the step env so the run
          # block stays pure shell — the retry REG
          # (test_bench_harbor_workflow.py::ZeroTrialRetryTest) executes
          # the block verbatim in a subprocess, where `${{ }}` would be a
          # bash bad substitution.
          SHARD_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD_INDEX: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1503 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).
          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"
          args=()
          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-i "$t"); done
          # Issue #1122 knobs, same env contract as bench.yml (shared
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py). gh-1556 AC2: the watch knobs now
          # ride the step env block on every shard (progress-watch is the
          # bench default), so the adapter always supervises — only
          # removing those exports restores the unsupervised run. The
          # inputs below stay meaningful ON TOP of the watch defaults:
          # an explicit agent-timeout clips the watch ceiling to base x4
          # (the pre-PR ladder semantics — under the watch the abs
          # ceiling is the cap that actually kills a progressing trial),
          # and an explicit progress-extension: false unsets the
          # step-env extension. With both inputs empty the step-env
          # watch values rule unchanged.
          # A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
            # gh-1556 rework: without this clip an operator-set base cap
            # would be silently ignored — under watch+extension the abs
            # ceiling alone bounds a progressing trial (base_sec is only
            # consulted with the extension off).
            # The watch exports are individually removable (the escape
            # hatch back to the legacy ladder): if the ceiling export
            # alone is gone, default it to base x4 under `set -u`
            # (exactly what the legacy ladder would have used) before
            # the clip — an unbound variable must not kill the shard.
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
          fi
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            ''|0|1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on|false|FALSE|False|no|off) ;;
            *) echo "::error::progress-extension must be boolean (true/false), got '$PROGRESS_EXTENSION'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            # gh-1556 rework: the step env exports FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1
            # (the watch default) — an explicit false must still win by
            # unsetting it, otherwise the input is a silent no-op.
            false|FALSE|False|no|off) unset FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION;;
            1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on) export FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1;;
          esac
          # gh-1658 C1: the harbor invocation + the zero-trial inline
          # retry. The job name stays pinned (one jobs/<name>/ dir per
          # shard, so the summary job's downloads cannot collide on
          # harbor's timestamped default; the family label keys results
          # per dataset version — fa-4.0-* matches the historical 4.0
          # names exactly) and is built from step-env matrix values so
          # the whole block remains pure shell.
          JOB_NAME="fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${SHARD_KIND}-${SHARD_INDEX}"
          run_harbor() {
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent \
              -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" \
              --job-name "$JOB_NAME" -o jobs \
              "${args[@]}"
          }
          # The zero-trial gate counts result.json PRESENCE anywhere
          # under the shard's job dir — the same presence rule the
          # summary's completeness count uses.
          trials_started() {
            [ -d "jobs/$JOB_NAME" ] || { echo 0; return 0; }
            find "jobs/$JOB_NAME" -name result.json | wc -l
          }
          if run_harbor; then
            :
          else
            harbor_status=$?
            if [ "$(trials_started)" -gt 0 ]; then
              # gh-1658 C1/AC2: a failure WITH trials is a real result —
              # never retried (a retry would double-bill and mix attempts).
              exit "$harbor_status"
            fi
            # gh-1658 C1/AC1: zero trials = a startup crash (docker /
            # rate-limit / dataset-resolve transient). Retry ONCE with
            # the same env/model/params; attempt 1's trial-less dir moves
            # aside so the retry owns the pinned job name and the failed
            # attempt's logs survive for RCA. The preserved dir never
            # matches the fa-<family>-* export globs (Hub upload +
            # summary family filter), so the merged export cannot
            # double-count its trials.
            mv "jobs/$JOB_NAME" "jobs/_attempt1-$JOB_NAME" 2>/dev/null || true
            if run_harbor; then
              echo "::warning::shard $JOB_NAME: zero-trial startup crash recovered by the inline retry (attempt 1 kept under jobs/_attempt1-$JOB_NAME)"
            else
              # gh-1658 C2: the marker keeps the RCA independent of job
              # logs surviving the rerun.
              {
                echo "## Shard $JOB_NAME"
                echo
                echo "zero-trial startup failure (retried once)"
              } >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/null}"
              exit 1
            fi
          fi

        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: harbor-job-shard-…

with:

      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

      # Same gate as bench.yml: stdlib-only bench script tests. Two
      # discovery roots: bench/terminal_bench (legacy scripts + the
      # harbor parity suite from #1122 — terminal-bench is installed
      # just for the legacy-adapter import surface) and bench/harbor_fa
      # (the #1124 family/summary suites + the #1123 token/cost summary
      # tests). Discovering bench/ itself would need __init__.py
      # plumbing the bench dirs don't have.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          pip install 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v

      # Download the dataset once for classification; harbor re-fetches
      # into its own cache during the run. DATASET is the canonical id
      # resolved by the family step (the raw input may be a bare label).
      - name: Shard dataset into CPU / GPU shards
        id: shards
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          SHARDS: ${{ inputs.shards }}
          CPU_ENV: ${{ inputs.cpu-env }}
        run: |
          harbor datasets download "$DATASET" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds" --overwrite
          # Dataset name at version: dir name is the dataset slug.
          ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds/$(basename "${DATASET%%@*}")"
          [ -d "$ds_dir" ] || ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds"
          # split_tasks.py writes the matrix/counts into GITHUB_OUTPUT itself.
          # harbor -i matches qualified ids (<org>/<name>): prefix with the
          # org part of the dataset spec.
          python bench/harbor_fa/split_tasks.py "$ds_dir" \
            --filter "$TASKS" --shards "$SHARDS" --cpu-env "$CPU_ENV" \
            --task-prefix "${DATASET%%/*}/"

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

- `Bench Harbor` shard step (`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`): when the harbor run fails with **zero** `result.json` files under the shard's job dir, the invocation is retried once inline (same env/model/params); a failure with ≥1 trial exits immediately — a real result, never retried.

# gh-1658: [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry on zero-trial startup crash (shard-12 lost 6% of run 38823577512)

## Description

## [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry when a shard crashes at startup with zero trials

### Product frame

A shard job that dies before its first trial is pure infra loss — it silently deletes ~6% of a full run's capacity and (if unnoticed) corrupts the aggregate. Run 38823577512 lost shard 12 this way: the "Run harbor" step failed after 12 s with zero trials started (docker/rate-limit/dataset-resolve transient — root cause unprovable, job log was lost to the rerun). Attempt 2 of the same shard ran fine (11/25). A transient startup crash must not cost a shard.

### Required capabilities

- **C1 — inline retry, zero-trial only.** In `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`, the shard job's harbor step: when the harbor run fails AND the shard's trial dir contains 0 `result.json` files, retry the harbor invocation once (same env/model/params). A failure WITH trials is a real result — never retried (it would double-bill and mix attempts).
- **C2 — explicit marker.** On a still-failing zero-trial shard, the step summary states `zero-trial startup failure (retried once)` so the RCA does not depend on job logs surviving.
- **C3 — aggregate guard.** The "Aggregate resolution rate" job fails loudly if any shard contributes 0 trials to the merged export (a shard that vanished from artifacts must not silently shrink the denominator).
- **C4 — docs.** `docs/bench.md` gets two lines: zero-trial retries once inline; a red shard with trials is a real result and is never auto-retried.

### Test matrix

- Workflow YAML lint / actionlint in CI (existing gates).
- Manual smoke: dispatch `tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1` and verify the retry branch is a no-op on success (no double trials in the export).
- The C3 aggregate guard is exercised by the existing summary scripts' empty-shard path (add a fixture if the merge script has none).

### Platform inventory

- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` (shard job harbor step + aggregate job).
- `docs/bench.md`.
- No Dart changes, no harness changes.

### Security

No new secrets, no new network paths; same container invocation retried.

### Acceptance

- [ ] AC1: a zero-trial startup failure retries once inside the same job and proceeds on success.
- [ ] AC2: a failure with ≥1 trial is never retried.
- [ ] AC3: aggregate job fails on any zero-trial shard.
- [ ] AC4: next full run loses no shard capacity to a startup transient without a visible retried-once marker.

          # gh-1576: the shard's external harness cap — the MIN of the
          # dataset-declared per-task agent timeouts (task.toml
          # `[agent] timeout_sec`, resolved pre-launch by split_tasks.py).
          # A shard where no task declares one emits NO key, which renders
          # as an empty env var = unknown: the knobs rule alone,
          # byte-identical (AC5, no invented clock — E1). When present,
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py folds it in via min() so fa's
          # deadline can never outlive harbor's per-task kill (I1) — the
          # adapter decides the kill at the cap and the audit names it
          # (outcome `external_cap`); a kill that still comes from
          # outside (harbor's wait_for / SIGTERM) flushes outcome
          # `external_kill` (I2).
          FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC: ${{ matrix.external_cap }}

          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}

          # gh-1503 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).

      - name: Shard dataset into CPU / GPU shards

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

Closes #1658
### What changed
- `Bench Harbor` shard step (`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`): when the harbor run fails with **zero** `result.json` files under the shard's job dir, the invocation is retried once inline (same env/model/params); a failure with ≥1 trial exits immediately — a real result, never retried.

- Retry gate keys on `result.json` **presence** under the shard job dir — the same presence rule the summary's completeness count uses.
- Attempt 1's trial-less dir is preserved under `jobs/_attempt1-<name>`: RCA evidence survives, and the name never matches the `fa-<family>-*` export globs, so the merged export / Hub upload cannot double-count.
- Still-failing zero-trial shard writes `zero-trial startup failure (retried once)` to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` — RCA no longer depends on job logs surviving.
- The harbor run block is pure shell (matrix identity rides step env `SHARD_KIND`/`SHARD_INDEX`), so `ZeroTrialRetryTest` **executes it verbatim** against a fake harbor: success = 1 invocation, no marker; zero-trial crash = exactly 1 retry with the same `--job-name`, proceeds on success; failure with trials = never retried.

## Description

## [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry when a shard crashes at startup with zero trials

### Product frame

A shard job that dies before its first trial is pure infra loss — it silently deletes ~6% of a full run's capacity and (if unnoticed) corrupts the aggregate. Run 38823577512 lost shard 12 this way: the "Run harbor" step failed after 12 s with zero trials started (docker/rate-limit/dataset-resolve transient — root cause unprovable, job log was lost to the rerun). Attempt 2 of the same shard ran fine (11/25). A transient startup crash must not cost a shard.

### Required capabilities

- **C1 — inline retry, zero-trial only.** In `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`, the shard job's harbor step: when the harbor run fails AND the shard's trial dir contains 0 `result.json` files, retry the harbor invocation once (same env/model/params). A failure WITH trials is a real result — never retried (it would double-bill and mix attempts).
- **C2 — explicit marker.** On a still-failing zero-trial shard, the step summary states `zero-trial startup failure (retried once)` so the RCA does not depend on job logs surviving.
- **C3 — aggregate guard.** The "Aggregate resolution rate" job fails loudly if any shard contributes 0 trials to the merged export (a shard that vanished from artifacts must not silently shrink the denominator).
- **C4 — docs.** `docs/bench.md` gets two lines: zero-trial retries once inline; a red shard with trials is a real result and is never auto-retried.

### Test matrix

- Workflow YAML lint / actionlint in CI (existing gates).
- Manual smoke: dispatch `tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1` and verify the retry branch is a no-op on success (no double trials in the export).
- The C3 aggregate guard is exercised by the existing summary scripts' empty-shard path (add a fixture if the merge script has none).

### Platform inventory

- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` (shard job harbor step + aggregate job).
- `docs/bench.md`.
- No Dart changes, no harness changes.

### Security

No new secrets, no new network paths; same container invocation retried.

### Acceptance

- [ ] AC1: a zero-trial startup failure retries once inside the same job and proceeds on success.
- [ ] AC2: a failure with ≥1 trial is never retried.
- [ ] AC3: aggregate job fails on any zero-trial shard.
- [ ] AC4: next full run loses no shard capacity to a startup transient without a visible retried-once marker.

# only arms its gap-aware decision under the extension).
          FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION: '1'
          FA_STALL_GAP_SEC: '360'
          FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC: '3600'
          # gh-1576: the shard's external harness cap — the MIN of the
          # dataset-declared per-task agent timeouts (task.toml
          # `[agent] timeout_sec`, resolved pre-launch by split_tasks.py).
          # A shard where no task declares one emits NO key, which renders
          # as an empty env var = unknown: the knobs rule alone,
          # byte-identical (AC5, no invented clock — E1). When present,
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py folds it in via min() so fa's
          # deadline can never outlive harbor's per-task kill (I1) — the
          # adapter decides the kill at the cap and the audit names it
          # (outcome `external_cap`); a kill that still comes from
          # outside (harbor's wait_for / SIGTERM) flushes outcome
          # `external_kill` (I2).
          FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC: ${{ matrix.external_cap }}
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
          # gh-1658 C1: the matrix identity rides the step env so the run
          # block stays pure shell — the retry REG
          # (test_bench_harbor_workflow.py::ZeroTrialRetryTest) executes
          # the block verbatim in a subprocess, where `${{ }}` would be a
          # bash bad substitution.
          SHARD_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD_INDEX: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1503 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).
          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"
          args=()
          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-i "$t"); done
          # Issue #1122 knobs, same env contract as bench.yml (shared
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py). gh-1556 AC2: the watch knobs now
          # ride the step env block on every shard (progress-watch is the
          # bench default), so the adapter always supervises — only
          # removing those exports restores the unsupervised run. The
          # inputs below stay meaningful ON TOP of the watch defaults:
          # an explicit agent-timeout clips the watch ceiling to base x4
          # (the pre-PR ladder semantics — under the watch the abs
          # ceiling is the cap that actually kills a progressing trial),
          # and an explicit progress-extension: false unsets the
          # step-env extension. With both inputs empty the step-env
          # watch values rule unchanged.
          # A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
            # gh-1556 rework: without this clip an operator-set base cap
            # would be silently ignored — under watch+extension the abs
            # ceiling alone bounds a progressing trial (base_sec is only
            # consulted with the extension off).
            # The watch exports are individually removable (the escape
            # hatch back to the legacy ladder): if the ceiling export
            # alone is gone, default it to base x4 under `set -u`
            # (exactly what the legacy ladder would have used) before
            # the clip — an unbound variable must not kill the shard.
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
          fi
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            ''|0|1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on|false|FALSE|False|no|off) ;;
            *) echo "::error::progress-extension must be boolean (true/false), got '$PROGRESS_EXTENSION'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            # gh-1556 rework: the step env exports FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1
            # (the watch default) — an explicit false must still win by
            # unsetting it, otherwise the input is a silent no-op.
            false|FALSE|False|no|off) unset FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION;;
            1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on) export FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1;;
          esac
          # gh-1658 C1: the harbor invocation + the zero-trial inline
          # retry. The job name stays pinned (one jobs/<name>/ dir per
          # shard, so the summary job's downloads cannot collide on
          # harbor's timestamped default; the family label keys results
          # per dataset version — fa-4.0-* matches the historical 4.0
          # names exactly) and is built from step-env matrix values so
          # the whole block remains pure shell.
          JOB_NAME="fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${SHARD_KIND}-${SHARD_INDEX}"
          run_harbor() {
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent \
              -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" \
              --job-name "$JOB_NAME" -o jobs \
              "${args[@]}"
          }
          # The zero-trial gate counts result.json PRESENCE anywhere
          # under the shard's job dir — the same presence rule the
          # summary's completeness count uses.
          trials_started() {
            [ -d "jobs/$JOB_NAME" ] || { echo 0; return 0; }
            find "jobs/$JOB_NAME" -name result.json | wc -l
          }
          if run_harbor; then
            :
          else
            harbor_status=$?
            if [ "$(trials_started)" -gt 0 ]; then
              # gh-1658 C1/AC2: a failure WITH trials is a real result —
              # never retried (a retry would double-bill and mix attempts).
              exit "$harbor_status"
            fi
            # gh-1658 C1/AC1: zero trials = a startup crash (docker /
            # rate-limit / dataset-resolve transient). Retry ONCE with
            # the same env/model/params; attempt 1's trial-less dir moves
            # aside so the retry owns the pinned job name and the failed
            # attempt's logs survive for RCA. The preserved dir never
            # matches the fa-<family>-* export globs (Hub upload +
            # summary family filter), so the merged export cannot
            # double-count its trials.
            mv "jobs/$JOB_NAME" "jobs/_attempt1-$JOB_NAME" 2>/dev/null || true
            if run_harbor; then
              echo "::warning::shard $JOB_NAME: zero-trial startup crash recovered by the inline retry (attempt 1 kept under jobs/_attempt1-$JOB_NAME)"
            else
              # gh-1658 C2: the marker keeps the RCA independent of job
              # logs surviving the rerun.
              {
                echo "## Shard $JOB_NAME"
                echo
                echo "zero-trial startup failure (retried once)"
              } >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/null}"
              exit 1
            fi
          fi

        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: harbor-job-shard-…

with:

      # Pinned: the adapter targets the 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent contract.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

      # discovery roots: bench/terminal_bench (legacy scripts + the
      # harbor parity suite from #1122 — terminal-bench is installed
      # just for the legacy-adapter import surface) and bench/harbor_fa
      # (the #1124 family/summary suites + the #1123 token/cost summary
      # tests). Discovering bench/ itself would need __init__.py
      # plumbing the bench dirs don't have.
      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
        run: |
          pip install 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v

      # Download the dataset once for classification; harbor re-fetches
      # into its own cache during the run. DATASET is the canonical id
      # resolved by the family step (the raw input may be a bare label).
      - name: Shard dataset into CPU / GPU shards
        id: shards
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          SHARDS: ${{ inputs.shards }}
          CPU_ENV: ${{ inputs.cpu-env }}
        run: |
          harbor datasets download "$DATASET" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds" --overwrite
          # Dataset name at version: dir name is the dataset slug.
          ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds/$(basename "${DATASET%%@*}")"
          [ -d "$ds_dir" ] || ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds"
          # split_tasks.py writes the matrix/counts into GITHUB_OUTPUT itself.
          # harbor -i matches qualified ids (<org>/<name>): prefix with the
          # org part of the dataset spec.
          python bench/harbor_fa/split_tasks.py "$ds_dir" \
            --filter "$TASKS" --shards "$SHARDS" --cpu-env "$CPU_ENV" \
            --task-prefix "${DATASET%%/*}/"

    needs: [setup, bench]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

The comment above says this gate uses "the same presence rule the summary's completeness count uses", but the two are not identical:

The divergence only matters if a crashed run ever leaves a deeply-nested `result.json` (e.g. an extracted archive or cache dir inside the job dir): the gate would then report "trials started", skip the inline retry, and the summary would still count 0 trials for that shard — so the shard is lost anyway, just without the retry chance. # gh-1658: [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry on zero-trial startup crash (shard-12 lost 6% of run 38823577512)

## Description

## [GOAL] harbor shard jobs: inline retry when a shard crashes at startup with zero trials

### Product frame

A shard job that dies before its first trial is pure infra loss — it silently deletes ~6% of a full run's capacity and (if unnoticed) corrupts the aggregate. Run 38823577512 lost shard 12 this way: the "Run harbor" step failed after 12 s with zero trials started (docker/rate-limit/dataset-resolve transient — root cause unprovable, job log was lost to the rerun). Attempt 2 of the same shard ran fine (11/25). A transient startup crash must not cost a shard.

### Required capabilities

- **C1 — inline retry, zero-trial only.** In `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`, the shard job's harbor step: when the harbor run fails AND the shard's trial dir contains 0 `result.json` files, retry the harbor invocation once (same env/model/params). A failure WITH trials is a real result — never retried (it would double-bill and mix attempts).
- **C2 — explicit marker.** On a still-failing zero-trial shard, the step summary states `zero-trial startup failure (retried once)` so the RCA does not depend on job logs surviving.
- **C3 — aggregate guard.** The "Aggregate resolution rate" job fails loudly if any shard contributes 0 trials to the merged export (a shard that vanished from artifacts must not silently shrink the denominator).
- **C4 — docs.** `docs/bench.md` gets two lines: zero-trial retries once inline; a red shard with trials is a real result and is never auto-retried.

### Test matrix

- Workflow YAML lint / actionlint in CI (existing gates).
- Manual smoke: dispatch `tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1` and verify the retry branch is a no-op on success (no double trials in the export).
- The C3 aggregate guard is exercised by the existing summary scripts' empty-shard path (add a fixture if the merge script has none).

### Platform inventory

- `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` (shard job harbor step + aggregate job).
- `docs/bench.md`.
- No Dart changes, no harness changes.

### Security

No new secrets, no new network paths; same container invocation retried.

### Acceptance

- [ ] AC1: a zero-trial startup failure retries once inside the same job and proceeds on success.
- [ ] AC2: a failure with ≥1 trial is never retried.
- [ ] AC3: aggregate job fails on any zero-trial shard.
- [ ] AC4: next full run loses no shard capacity to a startup transient without a visible retried-once marker.

# only arms its gap-aware decision under the extension).
          FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION: '1'
          FA_STALL_GAP_SEC: '360'
          FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC: '3600'
          # gh-1576: the shard's external harness cap — the MIN of the
          # dataset-declared per-task agent timeouts (task.toml
          # `[agent] timeout_sec`, resolved pre-launch by split_tasks.py).
          # A shard where no task declares one emits NO key, which renders
          # as an empty env var = unknown: the knobs rule alone,
          # byte-identical (AC5, no invented clock — E1). When present,
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py folds it in via min() so fa's
          # deadline can never outlive harbor's per-task kill (I1) — the
          # adapter decides the kill at the cap and the audit names it
          # (outcome `external_cap`); a kill that still comes from
          # outside (harbor's wait_for / SIGTERM) flushes outcome
          # `external_kill` (I2).
          FA_EXTERNAL_CAP_SEC: ${{ matrix.external_cap }}
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
          # gh-1658 C1: the matrix identity rides the step env so the run
          # block stays pure shell — the retry REG
          # (test_bench_harbor_workflow.py::ZeroTrialRetryTest) executes
          # the block verbatim in a subprocess, where `${{ }}` would be a
          # bash bad substitution.
          SHARD_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          SHARD_INDEX: ${{ matrix.i }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # gh-1503 defense-in-depth behind the setup preflight: the
          # resolved key env var must carry the selected provider's key
          # (indirect expansion — the name came from the resolve step).
          provider_key="${FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV:?resolve step did not run}"
          provider_key_value="${!provider_key}"
          [ -n "$provider_key_value" ] || { echo "::error::provider key env $provider_key is empty — the selected provider's bench secret is not set"; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$provider_key_value" | base64 -w0)"
          args=()
          for t in $SHARD_TASKS; do args+=(-i "$t"); done
          # Issue #1122 knobs, same env contract as bench.yml (shared
          # bench/fa_agent_timeout.py). gh-1556 AC2: the watch knobs now
          # ride the step env block on every shard (progress-watch is the
          # bench default), so the adapter always supervises — only
          # removing those exports restores the unsupervised run. The
          # inputs below stay meaningful ON TOP of the watch defaults:
          # an explicit agent-timeout clips the watch ceiling to base x4
          # (the pre-PR ladder semantics — under the watch the abs
          # ceiling is the cap that actually kills a progressing trial),
          # and an explicit progress-extension: false unsets the
          # step-env extension. With both inputs empty the step-env
          # watch values rule unchanged.
          # A ceiling beyond a task's declared cap is
          # clipped by harbor's own per-task timeout (min of the two wins).
          if [ -n "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" ]; then
            case "$AGENT_TIMEOUT" in *[!0-9]*)
              echo '::error::agent-timeout must be integer seconds'; exit 1;; esac
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC="$AGENT_TIMEOUT"
            # gh-1556 rework: without this clip an operator-set base cap
            # would be silently ignored — under watch+extension the abs
            # ceiling alone bounds a progressing trial (base_sec is only
            # consulted with the extension off).
            # The watch exports are individually removable (the escape
            # hatch back to the legacy ladder): if the ceiling export
            # alone is gone, default it to base x4 under `set -u`
            # (exactly what the legacy ladder would have used) before
            # the clip — an unbound variable must not kill the shard.
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC:-$((AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4))}"
            export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC="$(( FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC < AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ? FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC : AGENT_TIMEOUT * 4 ))"
          fi
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            ''|0|1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on|false|FALSE|False|no|off) ;;
            *) echo "::error::progress-extension must be boolean (true/false), got '$PROGRESS_EXTENSION'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          case "$PROGRESS_EXTENSION" in
            # gh-1556 rework: the step env exports FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1
            # (the watch default) — an explicit false must still win by
            # unsetting it, otherwise the input is a silent no-op.
            false|FALSE|False|no|off) unset FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION;;
            1|true|TRUE|True|yes|on) export FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=1;;
          esac
          # gh-1658 C1: the harbor invocation + the zero-trial inline
          # retry. The job name stays pinned (one jobs/<name>/ dir per
          # shard, so the summary job's downloads cannot collide on
          # harbor's timestamped default; the family label keys results
          # per dataset version — fa-4.0-* matches the historical 4.0
          # names exactly) and is built from step-env matrix values so
          # the whole block remains pure shell.
          JOB_NAME="fa-${FAMILY}-${ENV_TYPE}-${SHARD_KIND}-${SHARD_INDEX}"
          run_harbor() {
            .bench-venv/bin/harbor run -d "$DATASET" -a fa_agent:FaAgent \
              -e "$ENV_TYPE" -m "$MODEL" -k "$ATTEMPTS" -n "$NCONC" \
              --job-name "$JOB_NAME" -o jobs \
              "${args[@]}"
          }
          # The zero-trial gate counts result.json PRESENCE anywhere
          # under the shard's job dir — the same presence rule the
          # summary's completeness count uses.
          trials_started() {
            [ -d "jobs/$JOB_NAME" ] || { echo 0; return 0; }
            find "jobs/$JOB_NAME" -name result.json | wc -l
          }
          if run_harbor; then
            :
          else
            harbor_status=$?
            if [ "$(trials_started)" -gt 0 ]; then
              # gh-1658 C1/AC2: a failure WITH trials is a real result —
              # never retried (a retry would double-bill and mix attempts).
              exit "$harbor_status"
            fi
            # gh-1658 C1/AC1: zero trials = a startup crash (docker /
            # rate-limit / dataset-resolve transient). Retry ONCE with
            # the same env/model/params; attempt 1's trial-less dir moves
            # aside so the retry owns the pinned job name and the failed
            # attempt's logs survive for RCA. The preserved dir never
            # matches the fa-<family>-* export globs (Hub upload +
            # summary family filter), so the merged export cannot
            # double-count its trials.
            mv "jobs/$JOB_NAME" "jobs/_attempt1-$JOB_NAME" 2>/dev/null || true
            if run_harbor; then
              echo "::warning::shard $JOB_NAME: zero-trial startup crash recovered by the inline retry (attempt 1 kept under jobs/_attempt1-$JOB_NAME)"
            else
              # gh-1658 C2: the marker keeps the RCA independent of job
              # logs surviving the rerun.
              {
                echo "## Shard $JOB_NAME"
                echo
                echo "zero-trial startup failure (retried once)"
              } >> "${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-/dev/null}"
              exit 1
            fi
          fi

        with:
          name: harbor-job-shard-…

      # tests). Discovering bench/ itself would need __init__.py

        run: |
          pip install 'terminal-bench==0.2.18'
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench -v
          python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v

      # Download the dataset once for classification; harbor re-fetches
      # into its own cache during the run. DATASET is the canonical id
      # resolved by the family step (the raw input may be a bare label).
      - name: Shard dataset into CPU / GPU shards
        id: shards
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          SHARDS: ${{ inputs.shards }}
          CPU_ENV: ${{ inputs.cpu-env }}
        run: |
          harbor datasets download "$DATASET" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds" --overwrite
          # Dataset name at version: dir name is the dataset slug.
          ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds/$(basename "${DATASET%%@*}")"

          # split_tasks.py writes the matrix/counts into GITHUB_OUTPUT itself.
          # harbor -i matches qualified ids (<org>/<name>): prefix with the
          # org part of the dataset spec.
          python bench/harbor_fa/split_tasks.py "$ds_dir" \
            --filter "$TASKS" --shards "$SHARDS" --cpu-env "$CPU_ENV" \
            --task-prefix "${DATASET%%/*}/"

    needs: [setup, bench]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

        with:

      # run completeness — every expected trial attempted — after the merged
      # artifact below is uploaded.

        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: harbor-jobs-merged
          path: jobs/

      - name: Resolution summary & verdict
        if: always()
        env:

          # gh-1503: pinned to the setup resolve step's outputs — the

All new tests pass. Now the exhaustive review pass. Let me scrutinize potential issues:

1. **`_shard_index` counts `modal` (GPU) shards too, but the shard step also creates `_attempt1-*` dirs — fine.**

2. **Potential collision: `shard_trials` keys only on the numeric suffix.** Job names: `fa-<family>-<env>-<kind>-<shard>`. Both CPU and GPU shards are numbered globally (0..N-1 across include). OK per split_tasks.py.

3. **Non-shard dirs in merged jobs/**: historical/legacy dirs like `fa-4.0-docker-12` — suffix parse `12`. `_attempt1-fa-...` dirs — suffix parse: `_attempt1-fa-2.1-docker-cpu-3` ends with `-3` → parsed as shard 3! Wait — does the family filter exclude it? In main: `job_dirs = [d for d in job_dirs if d.name.startswith(f"fa-{args.family}-")]`. `_attempt1-fa-2.1-docker-cpu-3` starts with `_attempt1-`, so it's filtered out when `--family` is passed. The workflow always passes `--family`. OK.

   But wait — what if the merged export contains OTHER runs' dirs not matching the family? Filtered. OK.

4. **`expected_shards` from matrix counts GPU shards too — consistent with shard_trials covering modal dirs.** OK.

5. **jq availability on ubuntu-latest summary job**: jq is preinstalled on GitHub-hosted runners. OK. But is MATRIX_JSON empty edge? If setup job failed, `needs.setup.outputs.matrix` would be empty and `jq` would fail with set -e → step fails. That's arguably correct (fail loud). Fine.

6. **`expected_shards=$(...)` arithmetic**: `expected_trials=$((EXPECTED_TASKS * ATTEMPTS))` pre-exists.

7. **The retry `mv` races**: `mv "jobs/$JOB_NAME" "jobs/_attempt1-$JOB_NAME" 2>/dev/null || true` — if harbor crashed and never created the dir, mv fails silently — fine. But what if `_attempt1-$JOB_NAME` already exists? Not possible in a fresh job.

8. **Artifact upload of `_attempt1-` dirs**: Upload step `path: jobs/` uploads everything including `_attempt1-*`. Then summary download merges them into `jobs/`. `_attempt1-` dirs don't match family prefix → excluded from trial rows and shard_trials. Comment in PR says "never matches the fa-<family>-* export globs". Confirmed by the family filter and hub upload glob `jobs/fa-${FAMILY}-*`. OK.

9. **Subtle: `find "jobs/$JOB_NAME" -name result.json | wc -l` counts ALL result.json files, including from partial trials.** The presence rule matches summary's completeness count — check `_trial_rows`/presence count uses the same rule? The comment says so; presence completeness counts dirs with result.json presumably. Let me quickly verify the summary presence rule counts the same way — actually the important thing is consistency claim. Minor.

10. **`harbor_status=$?`**: In bash, inside `else` after `if cmd; then`, `$?` is the exit status of `cmd`. Correct.

11. **Retry proceeds but the shard step overall succeeds — warning only.** The aggregate guard will still count trials; the recovered retry produced trials, so no guard failure. But C2 marker for *recovered* shards: ticket C2 says "On a still-failing zero-trial shard" — marker only needed there. OK.

12. **`SHARD_INDEX: ${{ matrix.i }}`** — matrix.i is a number; env values are strings — fine in shell.

13. **Zero-trial gate false negative possibility**: harbor could fail AFTER creating result.json-less trial dirs vs fail after writing results — presence rule handles it. What about harbor succeeding but producing zero result.json? Then `run_harbor` succeeds, no retry, but shard contributed 0 trials → aggregate guard catches it. Good — that's exactly C3.

14. **`--expected-shards` type=int with jq output**: jq outputs a number; fine.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

Closes #1658
### What changed
- `Bench Harbor` shard step (`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`): when the harbor run fails with **zero** `result.json` files under the shard's job dir, the invocation is retried once inline (same env/model/params); a failure with ≥1 trial exits immediately — a real result, never retried.

- Retry gate keys on `result.json` **presence** under the shard job dir — the same presence rule the summary's completeness count uses.
